youtube.title: Rust for vs while Loops + Ranges (0..5 vs 0..=5) 🦀 | Rust Day 13 #Shorts

scenes.say: Zero dot dot five stops at four. Add an equals sign, and it reaches five.
scenes.captions: 0..5 stops at 4. Add an equals sign, and it reaches 5.

scenes.heading: while
scenes.say: A while loop runs while the condition is true. While number isn't zero, it prints the number and subtracts one. Then, liftoff.
scenes.captions: A while loop runs while the condition is true. While number != 0, it prints the number and subtracts 1. Then, liftoff.

scenes.heading: for
scenes.say: To go through an array, use for. for x in a gives each item in order: ten, twenty, thirty. There's no index, so no way to go past the end.
scenes.captions: To go through an array, use for. for x in a gives each item in order: 10, 20, 30. There's no index, so no way to go past the end.

scenes.heading: Ranges
scenes.say: Ranges give for a sequence of numbers. Zero dot dot five is zero to four. With an equals sign, five is included. And dot rev counts backwards.
scenes.captions: Ranges give for a sequence of numbers. 0..5 is 0 to 4. With an equals sign, 5 is included. And .rev() counts backwards.

scenes.heading: Common mistake
scenes.sub: an index that goes too far
scenes.say: Now the classic while loop bug: less than or equal to three, on an array of three items.
scenes.captions: Now the classic while loop bug: <= 3, on an array of 3 items.

scenes.heading: It panics
scenes.caption: index out of bounds
scenes.say: It prints ten, twenty, thirty, then panics: index out of bounds. Rust stops instead of reading random memory.
scenes.captions: It prints 10, 20, 30, then panics: index out of bounds. Rust stops instead of reading random memory.

scenes.heading: Use for instead
scenes.label: a[3] blocked
scenes.say: With for x in a, this bug can't happen. That's why Rust developers reach for for first.
scenes.captions: With for x in a, this bug can't happen. That's why Rust developers reach for "for" first.

scenes.heading: Recap
items: for x in a: every item
scenes.say: Recap: while runs until its condition is false, for walks every item, and ranges stop before the end unless you add an equals sign.
